title: A New Lunar Crater: McGetchin
explanation:
# The Moon's Rare Cosmic Collision

A whale-sized space rock slammed into the Moon between April and May 2024, carving out a crater two soccer fields wide—an event so rare it only happens about once every 132 years, as captured by NASA's orbiting lunar observer. The impact blasted loose Moon dust into the surrounding area, creating a frigid zone around the warm crater that will help scientists understand how cosmic collisions reshape planetary surfaces and reshape our appreciation for Earth's protective atmosphere.
